generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, you meet competing explanations for the same behaviour or finding. You take each study apart to see its claim, evidence and method; you weigh the rival explanations against each other; and you draw them into a position of your own. The three skills run together whenever you argue from the research literature.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students write about explanations for a well-known effect. One describes each study in turn and leaves the explanations side by side. The other takes each study apart, weighs one explanation against another on how well it fits the evidence, then argues a position of their own. The second essay reads as psychology; the first reads as notes, and using the three skills together is why.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, analysis, evaluation and synthesis work best as one practice. You take a study apart, weigh its explanation against rivals, and build a position of your own from the research. Running the three skills together is what lets you argue from the literature rather than just report it.

check.body: A student takes an article apart into its claim and evidence, weighs it against a rival reading, then draws both into a claim of their own. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: The three critical skills working as one practice: analysis, then evaluation, then synthesis, each feeding the next.
_items.feedback: Yes. The student moved from taking the source apart, to weighing it, to building an argument.

_items.text: Only analysis, because the student began by taking the article apart.
_items.feedback: Analysis was the first move, but the student also weighed the reading and built a claim.

_items.text: Only summary, because the student used more than one source.
_items.feedback: Using sources together to build a claim is synthesis, not summary.

_items.text: Evaluation on its own, because the student compared two readings.
_items.feedback: Weighing the readings was evaluation, but it sat inside the fuller practice of all three skills.
